guideTitle: Best Robot Vacuums for Hardwood Floors (2026)
metaTitle: Best Robot Vacuums for Hardwood Floors (2026)
metaDescription: Six robot vacuums for hardwood compared on grit control, mop water flow, quiet wheels and brush design, so floors stay clean without new scratches.
expertTake: The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is the top pick because its FlexiArm mop reaches baseboards and its dock washes pads between rooms. The eufy 11S MAX is the value pick for dry dust on a budget. Anyone with unsealed or waxed boards should skip the mop and buy a vacuum-only machine.
introParagraphs: Hardwood looks easy for a robot, because there is no pile to fight. The real risks are different: loose grit that scratches the finish when a wheel rolls over it, and too much water on boards that are not fully sealed. A good hardwood robot pulls grit up before it can be dragged.

That makes brush design, edge reach and water control more important than raw suction. This guide ranks six machines by how kindly they treat a finished floor, and it says plainly which ones should stay dry.

products.name: Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro, 20,000 Pa, FlexiArm edge mop, wash-and-dry dock
products.description:
The Qrevo 2 Pro suits boards because it mops along the edges, where hardwood collects the most grime and where a round mop normally cannot reach. FlexiArm swings the mop out toward baseboards, and the dock washes the pad between rooms so you are not spreading old dirt across the grain. A dual zero-tangle system keeps hair from wrapping the roller.

It has 20,000 Pa, which is more than any hardwood floor needs, and it sits at the top of the price range here. The value is in the dock and the edge reach, not the suction label. Set against the Roomba 105 Combo it washes its own pad and extends its mop, and the extra cost is the dock.

Only use the wet mode on sealed boards. Wipe the wash tray weekly, rinse the dirty tank after each mop run, and replace pads before they harden. Check the roller for pebbles now and then, because a trapped stone is what scratches a finish. Most owners find that moving the robot to the hallway for its first run each week, when the floor has the most outdoor grit, spares the living room boards.
products.bestFor: Sealed hardwood homes that want edge mopping and a washing dock.
cons: Top price tier of the six
Wet mode is unsafe on unsealed wood

products.name: Dreame D20 Air Plus, 20,000 Pa, 4 L bag, 120-day dock, dual anti-tangle
products.description:
The D20 Air Plus is the dock-first choice for boards. A large 4 L bag is quoted at up to 120 days, so loose grit and dust disappear into a sealed container instead of lingering in an open bin. Dual anti-tangle brushes handle long hair, and a mop pad covers light wet work.

Its 20,000 Pa matches the Qrevo 2 Pro on paper, but the mop is a simple pad that you rinse by hand, which keeps it in a lower tier. On hardwood the pad suits damp dust and footprints, not heavy spills. If you mostly vacuum and mop occasionally, the large bag is the better trade. A sealed bag also keeps the grit out of the room air when it empties, which matters on a polished finish that shows every speck.

Because the dock never washes the pad, wash it by hand after each wet run and let it dry. Keep the main brush clear so hair does not drag grit across the floor, and check the bag at one month.
products.bestFor: Hardwood homes with pets that want rare dock visits.
pros: 4 L bag lasts up to 120 days
Mop pad included for light damp work
Lower price tier than the Qrevo
cons: Real bag life depends on shedding

products.name: Roborock Q7 L5, 8,000 Pa, LiDAR, dual anti-tangle, mop combo
products.description:
The Q7 L5 maps the floor with a laser and plans efficient rows, which on hardwood means fewer repeated passes over the same boards and less wheel travel across grit. Its main brush is shaped to shed hair and the side brush is zero-tangle. The mop is an attachment for damp wiping.

Priced below the Dreame D20 Air Plus, it has no dock, so you empty the bin by hand. The 8,000 Pa figure is modest, and on bare boards it is plenty. If your concern is a methodical route more than a dock, this is the cleanest value on the list. Its quiet mode keeps the wheels gentle, and the saved map lets you exclude a room with delicate boards entirely.

After each run, empty the bin so grit does not sit against the filter, and rinse the mop cloth after wet use. Wipe the laser window monthly. Dry the wheels if the robot has crossed a damp patch, since wet tyres leave tracks on a polished finish.
products.bestFor: Hardwood flats that want a methodical laser route on a low budget.
pros: Low price tier for a laser robot
cons: 8,000 Pa is the lowest of the premium group

products.name: iRobot Roomba 105 Combo, 7,000 Pa, AutoEmpty 75 days, ClearView LiDAR
products.description:
The 105 Combo brings a recognised dock and laser mapping to hardwood. A bag in the AutoEmpty base is quoted at up to 75 days, ClearView LiDAR maps rooms and a three-stage cleaning pass lifts grit before the mop pad follows. The mop plate attaches when you want a damp wipe.

Its suction is 7,000 Pa, a notch below the Roborock, and the mop is a plain pad. The practical difference on boards is small, and the dock is the draw. Set against the Roborock Q7 L5 it adds the dock but gives up some suction at a mid price tier.

Care is short: replace the bag when full, rinse the pad after each wet run and wipe the dock port. Take the mop plate off for dry runs, since a pad dragged dry can leave marks on a high-gloss finish. The three-stage action loosens grit before the suction pulls it in, which is the right order on a hard surface.
products.bestFor: Hardwood homes that want a brand-name laser dock.
pros: AutoEmpty dock for up to 75 days
cons: Mop does not scrub dried spills
Lower suction than the Roborock models

products.name: Tikom G8000 Max, 5,000 Pa, 450 ml bin, 300 ml tank, app and remote
products.description:
The G8000 Max is aimed squarely at hard floors, and the listing says so. A 450 ml bin and 300 ml tank share the body, it can run up to 150 minutes in quiet mode and either an app or a remote steers it. Quiet mode also keeps wheel speed gentle on a polished surface.

Its 5,000 Pa is the lowest figure here, and the lack of a dock keeps the price low. The small tank suits a flat, and a large open plan will need refills. Against the eufy 11S MAX it adds a mop and an app, and costs a little more.

Wash the cloth, fill the tank only with clean water and empty the bin after each run. Let the cloth dry between runs, because a damp pad shut in a robot can mark a wood finish with mildew smell. Refill with plain water only, since cleaning solutions can leave a film and some makers void warranties for additives.
products.bestFor: Hardwood flats that want a cheap vacuum and mop combo.
pros: Low price tier with a mop included
cons: Small 300 ml tank for large floors

products.name: eufy 11S MAX, 2.85 in slim, BoostIQ, 100 minutes on hardwood
products.description:
The 11S MAX is the dry-only pick for boards. It runs up to 100 minutes on hardwood, stays quiet, and BoostIQ raises suction within about 1.5 seconds when it meets a rug. At 2.85 in tall it slips under furniture where dust sits on the finish.

It has no mop, no map and no dock, so there is no water to worry about on an unsealed floor. Against the Tikom G8000 Max it costs less and runs quieter, but gives up wet cleaning. If your boards are waxed or older, a dry robot is the safest choice. Its small bin is the one chore to respect, so empty it daily if you have a dog that tracks in grit.

Empty the bin after each run so grit does not accumulate, rinse the filter and snip hair from the roller. A clean roller matters on wood because wrapped hair can hold a pebble against the floor.
products.bestFor: Waxed or older boards where only dry cleaning is safe.
pros: No water, so safe on unsealed wood

buyingCriteria.explanation: Water is the real risk to hardwood. A sealed or polyurethane finish tolerates a damp pad, and an oiled, waxed or unfinished floor does not. If you are unsure, test a wet cloth on a hidden spot, or choose a dry robot like the eufy 11S MAX.

Scratches on wood come from small stones and sand trapped under a wheel or in a brush, not from the robot itself. A sealed dock bag such as the Dreame D20 Air Plus 4 L holds grit away from the floor, and frequent bin emptying on bin-only models does the same. Check the roller each week for lodged pebbles.

A mop that drips constantly leaves puddles at seams. The Tikom G8000 Max uses a 300 ml tank, and the Roborock and Dreame docks meter water by app setting. Choose the lowest flow that cleans, and avoid soaking boards. Seams between planks are where water sneaks in, so a pass that leaves the floor visibly wet is already too much.

Hardwood collects dust along baseboards, where a round robot misses the last inch. The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro extends a FlexiArm mop, and others rely on a static side brush. Rooms with plenty of skirting gain the most.

Soft rubber tyres grip without marking, and quiet modes keep wheel speed gentle. The Tikom G8000 Max quotes a quiet mode runtime of 150 minutes. Dirty tyres leave tracks, so wipe them if they pick up residue.

A laser map plans straight rows and reduces repeated passes over the same boards. The Roborock Q7 L5 and Roomba 105 Combo both use laser mapping. Random-pattern robots like the eufy 11S MAX cover boards by pattern and are fine in small rooms.

specDecoder.meaning: A protective coat such as polyurethane that keeps water out of the wood. It decides whether a mop is safe.
specDecoder.watchFor: If your maker guidance says dry only, skip every mop here and pick the eufy 11S MAX.

specDecoder.meaning: The volume of clean water the robot carries. Bigger tanks cover more floor between refills.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Tikom G8000 Max carries 300 ml, which suits a flat but not an open plan.

specDecoder.meaning: An arm that extends the mop or brush to reach baseboards and corners. It improves edge coverage.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro carries it, and the other picks do not.

specDecoder.meaning: A dock that empties the bin into a sealed bag. It keeps grit away from the floor.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Roomba 105 Combo quotes up to 75 days and the Dreame D20 Air Plus up to 120 days.

specDecoder.meaning: A peak motor rating at the strongest mode. Bare boards rarely need it.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Qrevo 2 Pro and D20 Air Plus list 20,000 Pa and the Tikom G8000 Max lists 5,000 Pa.

howWeEvaluated.title: Finish safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked machines by how well they protect a floor finish, including dry-only options and metered water. The eufy 11S MAX is the safest for waxed boards. Combos were judged on how controllable the wet mode is.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grit handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at dock bags and brush design, because grit causes scratches. The Dreame 4 L bag and anti-tangle brushes scored well. Bin-only models were judged on bin size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Edge and route
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared edge reach and mapping. The Qrevo 2 Pro leads on edges, and the Roborock Q7 L5 and Roomba 105 Combo lead on routing. Pattern robots were credited for small rooms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mop quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared washing docks with hand-rinsed pads. The Qrevo 2 Pro washes its pad, while the rest rely on you. A light-duty mop is fine for dust but not for spills.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed repeated owner reports on scratches, streaks and leaking tanks. Patterns outweighed single complaints. Models with repeated leak reports were marked down. Streaks on a glossy finish were another recurring theme and were weighed the same way.

cards.label: Wet
cards.text: The Qrevo 2 Pro, Q7 L5, Roomba 105 Combo and Tikom G8000 Max mop. They suit sealed floors and cost more to maintain.

cards.label: Dry
cards.text: The eufy 11S MAX only vacuums, so it is safe on any finish. It cannot lift sticky spills.

howToChoose.note: Choose dry if the finish is unknown, and wet only on sealed boards.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A sealed bag or bin that is emptied often, a roller you can check for stones, soft tyres and a route that does not repeat. Sweep large debris before the first run.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Dreame D20 Air Plus keeps grit sealed in a 4 L bag. The eufy 11S MAX keeps water off the finish.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your boards are sealed and you mop weekly. The Qrevo 2 Pro washes the pad for you and reaches the edges.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly vacuum. The eufy 11S MAX or Tikom G8000 Max cost much less.

maintenance.why: A trapped pebble drags across the finish and leaves a scratch line. Pull the roller and look.

maintenance.interval: After runs or per the app
maintenance.why: Grit in a full bin spills under the wheels. The D20 Air Plus bag lasts up to 120 days as a best case.
A dirty pad spreads grime and can leave film on sealed wood. Dry it before storing.

faq.q: Can a robot vacuum scratch hardwood?
faq.a: The robot rarely does, but grit trapped under a wheel or brush can. Keep the roller clean and empty the bin often. Sweep large stones first.

faq.q: Is it safe to mop hardwood with a robot?
faq.a: Only on a sealed finish and at low water flow. Unfinished, oiled or waxed boards can be damaged. A dry robot is the safe fallback.

faq.q: Do I need strong suction on hardwood?
faq.a: No. Bare boards need little suction, and a brush that lifts grit matters more. The Tikom G8000 Max at 5,000 Pa cleans bare floors well.

faq.q: Which dock is best for hardwood?
faq.a: A sealed bag dock keeps grit contained, and the Dreame D20 Air Plus offers the longest interval. A washing dock suits mopping homes.

faq.q: Will robot wheels mark my floor?
faq.a: Clean rubber tyres do not. Residue can leave tracks, so wipe them monthly. Check after any wet pass.

faq.q: Is a laser map worth it on hardwood?
faq.a: It reduces repeated passes in large rooms. In a small room a pattern robot is fine. The Roomba 105 Combo and Roborock Q7 L5 offer maps.
